params.body:
The new item stood in the bar as **Menu.operations**. The navigation prints `trans('menu.<naam>')`
and a key without a translation prints itself.

The cause: its migration wrote the name into `language_lines`, exactly the way every menu item
before it did (Inzichten, Functies), and in the meantime the menu names had moved to
`resources/lang/<taal>/menu.php`. The row went into a table nothing reads any more. The five files
carry the name now: Werking, Fonctionnement, Operations, Betrieb, Funcionamiento.

**And the answer to "are the others all right": yes.** `MenuNamesTest` asks the question the screen
asks — for every menu row in the database, in every language, is there a word to show — and every
other item passes. Only this one was missing.

Two things about that test worth naming. It asks with the **fallback off** (`Lang::has($key,
$taal, false)`), because `trans()` in German quietly hands back the Dutch text when the German key
is missing, and a test that accepts that proves nothing beyond "the Dutch exists". And I checked it
bites by removing the German key again: it fails and names `de: menu.operations`.

The dead `language_lines` row from the earlier migration is left where it is. It is inert, and
rewriting a migration that has already run on production buys nothing.

params.title: Werking has a name in the menu, and every menu item is asked for one
